    "Repository and available skill-directory filename and text searches for Kestrel and skill instructions"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the requested API changes, compatibility constraints, and unresolved migration and deletion decisions.",

  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "Which clients use the API and what pagination entry point can they adopt? Discovery should first inspect repository consumers and available client documentation.",
      "changes": "The pagination interface and boundary-level acceptance checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume generic HTTP clients; retain the existing unparameterized list response and expose paging only through an explicit query parameter. Confidence: low.",
      "blocks": "Discovery of consumers blocks a verified compatibility claim; the recorded default permits further investigation."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "How should pagination coexist with the requirement that existing endpoints keep returning the same result? Discovery should first establish the current list contract and any consumer expectations.",
      "changes": "Whether and how pagination can be offered without changing existing responses.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve GET /users without paging parameters as the current complete array, and return an array for explicitly requested pages. Confidence: low because the requested paginator also produces metadata.",
      "blocks": "A settled contract is needed before finalizing pagination and its tests; discovery or the recorded default can settle it."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What are the create, delete, confirmation and paginated-list request and response contracts, including statuses and errors? Discovery should first check existing consumers and API conventions.",
      "changes": "HTTP methods, paths, body and query shapes, success responses, error codes and tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Tentatively use POST /users with name and email, DELETE /users/:id with an explicit confirmation signal, and array-shaped successful mutation responses containing the affected user; use JSON errors. Confidence: low; do not treat these choices as established contracts.",
      "blocks": "Final handler and contract tests require discovery or the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What does careful deletion require: an explicit confirmation, a reversible operation, concurrency protection, or another safeguard? Discovery should first find any client, policy or migration requirements.",
      "changes": "Deletion workflow, data retention and failure-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Require an explicit confirmation for each deletion and reject an absent or invalid confirmation without changing state; assume permanent deletion after confirmation. Confidence: low.",
      "blocks": "The deletion contract and its tests require a settled safeguard; discovery or the recorded default can settle it."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What page size and invalid-input rules are established for this API? Discovery should first inspect callers and documentation; the paginator itself requires a size and has no default.",
      "changes": "Default page size, input validation, error behavior and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use a page size of 10 and one-based positive integer page numbers; reject invalid input. Confidence: low because no usual size is documented in the inspected files.",
      "blocks": "Final pagination behavior and tests require discovery or the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "What identifier format, allocation, uniqueness and preservation rules does the Kestrel migration require? Discovery should first locate the migration's authoritative schema, mapping and ownership.",
      "changes": "ID generation, persisted representation, collision handling and migration acceptance tests.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Preserve existing numeric IDs and tentatively allocate increasing, never-reused numeric IDs across restarts. Confidence: low; this does not establish Kestrel compatibility.",
      "blocks": "A verified migration-compatible ID design and completion claim require authoritative migration evidence; unrelated discovery can proceed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Where may durable user data live, and what are the expected restart, concurrent-write and persistence-failure semantics? Discovery should first inspect the target runtime and its storage guarantees.",
      "changes": "Persistence location, write ordering, recovery behavior and durability tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume one server process with a local durable file, restore memory on restart, and report a failed mutation if persistence fails; do not claim multi-process safety. Confidence: low.",
      "blocks": "A reliable persistence design and target-specific verification require discovery or the recorded single-process default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Does the intended runtime provide a writable persistent location and retain the existing Node and port configuration? Discovery should first inspect the delivery environment.",
      "changes": "Storage configuration, startup behavior and deployment checks.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume Node 20 or newer, built-in modules only, and the existing PORT override with port 3000 as fallback; assume a writable durable local path only until verified. Confidence: medium for repository settings and low for target storage.",
      "blocks": "A target-specific durability claim requires runtime evidence; local design can proceed under the recorded assumption."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "What store and handler boundaries permit persistence, API handling and independent tests without adding dependencies? Discovery should first inspect the existing exports and skill instructions available to the delivery run.",
      "changes": "Module seams and the coordination boundary between handler and test work.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Retain the current store, paginator and server module boundaries, adding only the seams needed for isolated storage and HTTP tests. Confidence: medium.",
      "blocks": "Coordinated implementation and tests require an agreed interface; inspection or the recorded default can establish one."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which checks demonstrate CRUD, guarded deletion, preserved responses, paging including a short final page, and restart durability at their real boundaries? Discovery should first inspect the existing tests and accessible runtime.",
      "changes": "Test cases, test fixtures and completion evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use npm test and Node's built-in test runner, with HTTP boundary checks and a restart persistence check; add a short-final-page regression test. Confidence: high for the framework and medium for test design.",
      "blocks": "Completion requires passing boundary checks; the recorded default permits test design."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Where will the completed checkout be returned, and is a separate release target or access required? Discovery should first inspect the harness's delivery context.",
      "changes": "The final handoff and any release verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver to the named repository checkout at final return; no deployment target is specified. Confidence: medium.",
      "blocks": "A deployed availability claim requires a named target, access and a release; repository delivery can proceed under the recorded default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "Are there authentication, visibility or other security requirements for creating, listing and deleting users? Discovery should first inspect the runtime and consumer environment for existing controls.",
      "changes": "Access controls, data exposure and security tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume the existing API's deployment boundary provides any access control; the current server itself identifies no actors and exposes user records to any caller that can reach it. Confidence: low for deployment controls.",
      "blocks": "A security suitability claim requires environment evidence; the recorded default does not authorize inventing an authentication system."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can the requested improve, parallel handler-and-test work, and code review be carried out using the host's actual skill instructions and worker capabilities? Discovery should first locate those instructions and establish available execution access.",
      "changes": "The delivery workflow and evidence required before completion.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Treat all three as required later-stage activities; the host lists them, but their full instructions and execution availability were not verified in this intake. Confidence: high for the request and low for availability.",
      "blocks": "A claim that the requested workflow is complete requires the activities and their evidence; intake and independent discovery can proceed."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the Node users API in this repository; this unattended intake is read-only, starts no server, implements nothing and grants no broader scope. S2 [fact/open: Q3–Q4]: API consumers need user creation and guarded deletion; discovery or the recorded defaults must settle their contracts and deletion safeguard before those are finalized. S3 [fact/open: Q1–Q2, Q5, Q10]: List paging must use the existing paginator and its short final page must be checked; inspection shows its floor-based page count omits a nonempty partial final page, and neither a default page size nor a list paging contract is established. S4 [fact]: Keep the project dependency-free and straightforward. S5 [fact/open: Q7–Q8]: Keep users in memory while making changes survive restart; discovery must establish durable storage and concurrency conditions before a target-specific durability claim. S6 [fact/open: Q9–Q10, Q13]: A later delivery run must conduct parallel handler and test work, repeat improve until it finds only trivial changes, and complete code review; skill availability and evidence remain to be established. S7 [fact/open: Q6]: Preserve IDs for the next-quarter Kestrel migration; discovery must find the authoritative migration contract before compatibility can be claimed. S8 [fact]: The current server uses PORT when set to a usable number and otherwise port 3000. S9 [fact/open: Q2–Q3]: The current list returns a JSON array of user objects, whereas the paginator returns an object with page, pages and items; discovery or recorded defaults must settle how mutation and paginated responses honor the requested shape. S10 [fact/open: Q2]: Preserve existing endpoint responses, including the unparameterized list and individual-user lookup; discovery must resolve the paging compatibility boundary. Interaction and state [facts/assumptions: Q1, Q7, Q12]: Callers interact through HTTP; the server has no actor identification or authentication in the inspected code, and its in-memory users are shared by callers of one process and disappear on restart. Assume no session-specific state, no cross-process coordination and no additional visibility restrictions until discovery establishes them; these defaults do not establish multi-process safety or access control. Source hints [leads, not verified facts]: inspect the repository and tests, the host's listed skill instructions and delivery context, and any accessible Kestrel migration team, owner, workspace, channels, internal documentation or private repository discovered from those sources; no specific such location or owner was identified. Sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. Delivery and visibility [fact/assumption: Q11]: The named repository is the authorized result location; an isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and any separately deployed outcome exists only after release. No deployment target was named."
}
